parts.note: read literally, the foundation of tending a garden is working the soil; in everyday use the phrase names preliminary preparation for any project

explanation.surface: A question about what lies at the heart of horticulture.
explanation.definitionFit: Preliminary work that everything else rests on is literally, for a gardener, digging the earth.

definitions.meaning: available, as in the best deal currently on offer
working, operating, as in a concern that is up and running

explanation.surface: Being had while in the thick of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Available, as in the best price on offer; and operating, as in a thriving business.

definitions.meaning: a hand is a worker, a factory employee
effective or in force, as a rule that is currently valid

explanation.surface: A piece of practical help.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory worker is a hand; and something in force or effective is functioning in practice.

clue.text: Ann, alarmed then confused by the old-timer

indicators.note: mixed up, so these fourteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ann takes fright and is then bewildered by an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: This extinct prehistoric human is an old-timer in the deepest sense.

clue.text: Greedy owl, unsettled on perch, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other
the bird's letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: a perch is an example of a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A hungry bird is restless on its roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' turns OWL into WOL, placed on top of FISH; 'perhaps' shows perch is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous like a hungry wolf, so voracious or grasping.

clue.text: Most hopeful, so tries to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: An optimist makes an effort to turn over a new leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose-tinted outlooks are optimistic, so the superlative means most optimistic.

definitions.meaning: to plump down is to drop heavily, sit down with a thud
a show or venture that does badly

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a dud option.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop down heavily is one sense, and a theatrical or commercial dud is the other.

definitions.meaning: a ... corporal is the lowest NCO rank in the British Army

explanation.surface: A question about the kind of NCO someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: Lance corporal is the British Army's most junior non-commissioned rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The word pairs with corporal for a junior army rank, and is also a boy's given name.

clue.text: What, in effect, keeps one's head above water

definitions.text: What, in effect, keeps one's head above water

parts.words: What, in effect, keeps one's head above water
parts.note: the idiom means staying afloat financially, but here a submarine's viewing tube literally puts the viewer's eye above the surface

explanation.surface: Something that helps a person stay solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's optical tube lets a submerged crew see above the surface.

parts.note: wormwood is a bitter herb, and a byword for bitterness
scrubs means cleans hard

explanation.surface: A sour mood leads someone to scour the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The can' is slang for prison; Wormwood Scrubs is a prison in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is slang for jail, and this is a well-known London jail.

clue.text: Skating mishap where the glacier's steep

definitions.meaning: a tumble on the rink, read as two words
a steep section of a glacier where the ice breaks up like a frozen waterfall

explanation.surface: A skater comes a cropper on a steep stretch of mountain ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a tumble on the rink; as one it is the steep, broken part of a glacier.

clue.text: New College warden left Jenny a moke

parts.note: swap the first letters of Jenny and moke and the phrase becomes left many a joke, the kind of slip this Oxford don was famous for

explanation.surface: An Oxford head bequeaths a donkey to someone called Jenny.
explanation.walkthrough: A jenny is a female donkey and a moke is a donkey, so the surface is literally true; the phrase is also a sound-swap of 'left many a joke', the warden's legacy.
explanation.definitionFit: William Spooner, famous for transposing initial sounds, was Warden of New College, Oxford.

clue.text: Old man shows a way to ring the changes

definitions.text: a way to ring the changes
definitions.meaning: one of the standard methods of change-ringing on church bells

explanation.surface: An elderly gent demonstrates how to vary things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring the changes' is meant literally: change-ringing is the English art of ringing church bells in shifting orders, and Grandsire is one of its classic methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is an old forefather, and Grandsire is a named bell-ringing method.

clue.text: They say beef and mutton are enjoyed by many in the pink

definitions.text: enjoyed by many in the pink

indicators.note: the setter tells us the following words are only as people pronounce them

parts.note: both are kinds of butcher's flesh, cuts sold for the table

explanation.surface: Diners in fine fettle relish roasts of cattle and sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' means hunting pink, the red coat of a British fox-hunter; hunts gather at events of this name. 'are' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox-hunting gatherings are the occasions riders in red coats look forward to.

parts.note: suggests the clamour of an uprising, but means the sound something spinning makes

explanation.surface: The din of a political uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapidly spinning wheel or propeller gives off a buzzing hum.

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club
to cock is to raise or set upright, as a hat brim or a gun's hammer

explanation.surface: A society organises its feathered friends.
explanation.definitionFit: These are long-billed game birds of woodland.

clue.text: A controversial issue may come up at dinner

definitions.meaning: a delicate subject that no one wants to handle
literally a steaming spud served at the meal

explanation.surface: A touchy subject gets raised over the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject too delicate to handle is the figurative sense; a steaming baked spud on the plate is the literal one.

explanation.surface: Being ready to help is pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: It means pleasant company, and also ready to consent to a proposal.

definitions.meaning: rock that juts out beyond the vertical, a hazard to climbers
as a verb, to beetle is to jut out or project, as beetling brows or cliffs do

explanation.surface: Insects have difficulty scaling things.
explanation.definitionFit: Projecting rock is a mountaineer's challenge, and to beetle is to jut out over something.

indicators.note: badly made, so the letters are shuffled into new shape

explanation.surface: A complaint about a fastener and shoddy classification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is a slang word for a miser; 'with' links; 'poor' rearranges GRADING.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw, in old slang, is a tight-fisted person, a miser.

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail of an animal
N and S are two points of the compass, north and south

explanation.surface: Retracing a path around a couple of spots.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or venture is to support it, especially with money.

indicators.note: a set-back thing is put in reverse, so the pieces before it read from right to left

parts.note: a grid is a network, such as the national electricity grid

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans a failure in the power supply of the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns E plus GRID round to give DIRGE; 'the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful song for the dead is a musical lament.

indicators.note: only the leading half of the word's letters is kept

parts.note: camelopard is an old name for the giraffe

explanation.surface: The forequarters of a tall African animal that chews the cud.
explanation.walkthrough: Camelopard is a ten-letter archaic name for the giraffe; 'front half of' keeps its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This humped desert animal chews the cud, like cattle and sheep.

parts.note: Shylock's scornful question to Antonio about lending; fill the gap with the missing word

explanation.surface: A gapped quotation from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock asks 'Hath a dog money? Is it possible a cur can lend three thousand ducats?'
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock mocks Antonio's request for a loan by asking whether a cur has any cash.

parts.note: not a wrapped present but the festive merriment and feasting the season brings every year

explanation.surface: A present given every December.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive merriment and hearty food are what the season hands out every year.

indicators.note: of poor quality, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A meagre portion set aside for big flightless birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large flightless South American birds, sometimes called South American ostriches.

parts.note: can, as in you can go, means you may
ta-ta is a colloquial farewell

explanation.surface: A piece for choir with a farewell to someone named May.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a composition for voices, often sacred, with chorus and soloists.

clue.text: Trip with a pole and fall

parts.note: S stands for south, one of the earth's poles
to tumble is to fall

explanation.surface: Someone goes vaulting and comes down hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links the definition to the wordplay; a pole is S (south), not a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's footing is to trip.

indicators.note: a ringing sound is something heard, so the word for the welkin is taken as spoken

parts.note: welkin is a poetic word for the heavens above

explanation.surface: An island so loud it makes the heavens resound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' links. The Isle of Skye is in the Scottish Hebrides; welkin is an old poetic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: If all goes well they should get the post

definitions.text: If all goes well they should get the post

parts.words: If all goes well they should get the post
parts.note: sounds like job candidates hoping for an appointment, but means people whose letters are delivered

explanation.surface: Hopeful applicants expect to land the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Those named on envelopes are the ones the mail is meant for.
